hero: In a nephrology clinic in San Fernando, Pampanga, a Filipino nephrology fellow in a white coat sits at a table with a tired-looking man in his late thirties and his younger brother, who holds a passport; their mother sits beside them; a transplant referral checklist lies on the table; warm afternoon light through jalousie windows, serious but hopeful mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Refer transplant-eligible patients early and run recipient and donor evaluations in parallel.
figures.content: Vertical flowchart. Box 1 'Progressive CKD, kidney failure expected' with note 'Use eGFR trend and kidney failure risk'. Box 2 'Raise transplant at first visit; ask about willing relatives'. Box 3 'Refer at least 6-12 months before anticipated dialysis (KDIGO 2020, Not Graded)'. Then two parallel columns: left 'Recipient evaluation' with icons for Immunologic (ABO, HLA, crossmatch), Cardiac, Infection (HIV, hepatitis B and C, TB, strongyloides), Cancer, Frailty/BMI, Adherence and psychosocial; right 'Living donor evaluation (separate team member)'. Both converge on 'Transplant team decision'. Final split: 'Pre-emptive living-donor transplant (preferred)' and 'Deceased-donor list via PHILNOS'. Side note: 'Plan dialysis access anyway'.

figures.teaches: Living donor suitability rests on a whole-person risk estimate with explicit KDIGO 2017 thresholds and protected consent.
figures.content: Card with numbered steps. 1 'Voluntary? Interview alone, freedom to withdraw'. 2 'GFR' as a three-band bar: green '90 or more: acceptable', amber '60-89: individualize', red 'below 60: should not donate' (mL/min per 1.73 m2). 3 'Albuminuria' bar: green 'below 30 mg/day', amber '30-100', red 'above 100'. 4 'Blood pressure: normal acceptable; controlled to systolic below 140 may be acceptable'. 5 'Diabetes: type 1 should not donate; type 2 individualize'. 6 'Lifetime risk estimate vs program threshold'. 7 'Consent without recipient present'. 8 'Yearly BP, albuminuria, creatinine/eGFR after donation'. Footer strip: '15-year kidney failure: 30.8 vs 3.9 per 10,000 (Muzaale 2014)'.

card: Two Filipino brothers seated side by side in a clinic corridor, one holding a passport, soft daylight, no text.
